newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - June 26.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - June 26.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Thursday :

* The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 68.08 points to 7,689.98 as blue-chip stocks and bonds fell on Wednesday as crude oil prices shot up, reviving fears of inflation and rising U.S. interest rates.
* On Wednesday, OPEC talks in Vienna resulted in an agreement to try to rescue weak oil prices by extending a freeze on the cartel's production quotas until the end of the year.
* The World Bank said on Wednesday it had approved a $66.4 million credit to help finance renewable energy sources in Indonesia.

* On Wednesday, the Jakarta Composite Index closed down 0.13 percent at 712.50 points after hitting an intra-day low of 708.67 points on bargain-hunting in blue chips led by Telkom and Sampoerna, brokers said.
* On Thursday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,431.50/32.50 at 0110 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,431.00/32.00.
* Cigarette stocks Hanjaya Mandala Sampoerna and Gudang Garam on investor concern over a slowdown in the growth in the industry.

* Also on market talk of a possible swap of shares between HM Sampoerna's founder -- Putera Sampoerna -- and a major shareholder of the Salim group conglomerate. Both groups have stakes in noodle maker Indofood and Astra International.
* Energy firm PT Medco Energy after Bisnis Indonesia newspaper reported on Thursday that the firm had provided $60 million to take a stake in Britain's Dragon Oil . No details were available.
* Engineering firm Bukaka Teknik Utama after president director Fadel Muhammad reportedly indicated the firm was considering strategic alliances with foreign firms. He gave no details.
* Pulp and paper maker PT Indah Kiat after its notes and yen bond were rated BB- by Standard and Poor's.
* Paper maker Tjiwi Kimia after it said it expected to post a 1997 net profit around 30 percent higher than the previous year.

* Property firm Duta Anggada after the firm won shareholders' approval to split the nominal value per share to 500 rupiah from 1,000 rupiah, and its plan to invest $400 million in new property projects in the next four years.
* Alumunium producer Alumindo Light Metal Industry following a report that it expected to book net profit of 44 billion rupiah for 1997 from 20.6 billion rupiah in 1996.
* Property firm PT Jakarta International Hotel Development (JIHD) on reports that it will increase its stake in cellular phone operator Satelindo to 25 percent from the current 21.37 percent.
* Bakrie Land Development following reports that it would invest 130 billion rupiah to develop a 340-hectare integrated tourism and industrial area in Lampung, Sumatra.
